text:
Ari (CS): FYI filing this here so ENG/ML/SRE can triage. Customer (Acme) reports a regression after last week's rollout. They say identical prompts are getting inconsistent outputs within the same session — sometimes "terse/old" style, sometimes "verbose/new". Ticket SUP-8123 attached.

Ari (CS): Repro summary from customer (copied):
1) Send same user prompt 10x in session.
2) Expect consistent persona (concise assistant).
3) Observed ~7/10 concise, 3/10 verbose; variability appears correlated with time-of-request but not prompt content.

Examples from customer (two samples):
---
Prompt: "Summarize the following API change in 2 bullet points."
Response A (expected concise): "- Deprecates v1 tokens endpoint.
- Use /v2/tokens with new auth header."

Response B (unexpected verbose): "The API team has decided to deprecate the old tokens endpoint in favor of /v2/tokens. This will affect integrations that rely on the legacy header; please migrate to the new Authorization scheme described below..."
---

Ari (CS): They also provided a simple curl repro they used: 
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <KEY>" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -d '{"model":"redwood-alpha-1","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Summarize the following API change in 2 bullet points."}],"session_id":"acme-session-42"}'
```

Marcus (Support): I checked request IDs they sent in the ticket: rqs-7744, rqs-7747, rqs-7751. All come from same session_id and same client IP. They also pasted SDK debug with routing header present. No auth or billing errors. Only content/behavior mismatch.

Devon (SRE): Dumped routing debug for those request IDs — looks like our smart-routing policy triggered fallback to a quantized variant for some requests due to transient capacity signals. Key lines from routing log: 
```
[2026-03-14T17:02:11Z] route_decision trace=rq:rqs-7744 policy=cost-aware selected=redwood-alpha-1 primary=true
[2026-03-14T17:02:12Z] route_decision trace=rq:rqs-7747 policy=cost-aware selected=redwood-alpha-1-quant primary=false (fallback) reason=capacity_burst
[2026-03-14T17:02:13Z] route_decision trace=rq:rqs-7751 policy=cost-aware selected=redwood-alpha-1 primary=true
```
Devon (SRE): So 7747 was routed to the quantized variant (model suffix "-quant") which has slightly different output distribution due to post-quantization tokenization/kernels. That explains inconsistent style.

Lena (ML Eng): Thanks — that matches hypothesis. The quantized variant was onboarded for cost saving and is fully compatible for general prompts but we haven't validated strict persona preservation for short instructional prompts. We should treat this as a quality regression for this customer.

Marcus (Support): Customer wants either a fix (consistent outputs) or ability to pin to a single model variant per session. They said this inconsistency breaks content moderation heuristics downstream.

Lena (ML Eng): Short term options:
- Pin the customer's session to the non-quantized model (redwood-alpha-1) via routing override.
- Disable cost-aware fallback for their org id for now.
- Run a quick eval suite on alpha-1 vs alpha-1-quant for the customer's prompt set to quantify divergence.

Devon (SRE): I can set a routing override at the account level. Proposed command: 
```json
{
  "org_id": "acme-corp",
  "override": {
    "primary_model": "redwood-alpha-1",
    "allow_fallbacks": false
  }
}
```
I'll apply it to the canary pool and confirm.

Ari (CS): Customer asked for repro steps so we can confirm when the override is live (they will re-run their 10x loop).

Lena (ML Eng): I'll run a quick diff on their sample prompts to measure token-level divergence and flag any hallucination/regression signals. If we find material regressions from quantization, we'll schedule revert for that variant until we can fix calibration. Filed INF-2345 to track follow-up.

rollout-bot: Canary rollback scheduled for model variant redwood-alpha-1-quant on canary pool at 2026-03-15T02:00:00Z (initiated by Lena).

ops-bot: Routing override applied for org=acme-corp, override_id=ovr-9921 (allow_fallbacks=false).

Devon (SRE): Confirmed after override: for rqs-rerun-1..10 the route_decision shows primary selected every time. Pasting short log: 
```
[2026-03-14T18:12:01Z] route_decision trace=rq:rqs-rerun-3 policy=account-override selected=redwood-alpha-1 primary=true
[2026-03-14T18:12:02Z] route_decision trace=rq:rqs-rerun-7 policy=account-override selected=redwood-alpha-1 primary=true
```
Devon (SRE): Customer re-ran their 10x loop and confirmed consistent concise outputs.

Marcus (Support): Customer is satisfied with the temporary workaround but wants permanent options: either stronger semantic compatibility guarantees for model variants or an API-level session pinning feature.

Lena (ML Eng): Agreed. Action items:
- INF-2345: Evaluate quantized variant for persona-preservation; recommended changes or revert. (Lena)
- OPS-1178: Add org-level routing pinning API + session pin header docs (Devon + Marcus)
- CS-Note: Communicate timeline to Acme and close SUP-8123 once infra stable (Ari)

Ari (CS): I'll follow up with the customer tomorrow with the rollback confirmation and the plan. Thanks all :thumbsup:

Marcus (Support): Logging here for timeline — estimated SLA impact: low; customer impact immediate but mitigated. Will keep ticket open until INF-2345 resolved.

Lena (ML Eng): I'll attach evaluation artifacts to INF-2345 once ready. Expect initial results in 24 hrs.

ops-bot: Note: related rollout "alpha-variants-cost-save" shows 3% increased selection of quantized variants during peak in last deploy window.

Ari (CS): Closing notes: root cause = routing policy + quantized variant behavioral drift. Short-term mitigation = account-level override/pinning + canary rollback. Long-term = improve variant validation and add session-level pinning API to avoid mixed-variant sessions.
